title: Night Count Required in a Modem- or Card-Proven Download Window — PAP Supply Replenishment Program
content:
**Data note.** For a PAP device of a class whose compliance is proven only from modem or card data (a device class of PAP Therapy Equipment), the number of nights a compliance download's window must hold, when the download is read as proof of continued use for the PAP Supply Replenishment Program, depends on how soon the download was taken after the last night of its window:

- **21 nights** when the download was taken no more than 7 days after the last night of its window;
- **25 nights** when the download was taken more than 7 days after that night.

For any other device class, no such modem or card night count applies.

## Counting the delay

The delay is the number of days from the last night of the download's window to the date the download was taken, both as recorded on the device record.

| Device class's compliance proven only from modem or card data | Days from the last night of the window to the date taken | Nights the window must hold |
|---|---|---|
| yes | 0 to 7 | 21 |
| yes | 8 or more | 25 |
| no | any | no modem or card night count |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

- Last night of the window on the 4th, download taken on the 11th: 7 days, so 21 nights.
- Last night of the window on the 4th, download taken on the 12th: 8 days, so 25 nights.

## Example (hypothetical)

A download from a device whose class proves compliance only from modem or card data, taken 3 days after its window closed, shows 23 nights in its window: 23 nights reach the 21-night count. The same download taken 10 days after its window closed would need 25 nights and would fall short.
